guitar.evidence: Dave Mustaine's Dean V signature (VMNT/Flying V) is iconic and well documented as his main instrument for most of Megadeth's career (after early Jackson King V years).
guitar.notes: Raised confidence to high since Mustaine's Dean V signature is genuinely iconic; simplified model list to focus on the most documented instrument.

tone.target: dry thrash crunch with tight palm-mutes
tone.profile: dry thrash crunch with tight palm-mutes
tone.summary: A tight, high-gain signal chain using a Boost for attack, Distortion for crunch, and an aggressive Marshall-style amp paired with a 4x12 cabinet to achieve percussive thrash tones.

blocks.purpose: Eliminate hum and noise inherent in high-gain thrash tones.
Provide a tight, aggressive boost to enhance pick attack and punch for palm-muted riffs.

alternatives.reason: Good alternative for grit, but 'Boost' is better for pure tightness.

blocks.purpose: Establish the core high-gain crunch required for thrash metal without excessive fuzz.

alternatives.reason: Could work, but 'Distortion' offers a more balanced modern high-gain tone.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall/JCM-style punch and aggressive midrange needed for thrash.

alternatives.reason: Also suitable, but UK 50 often provides a slightly more modern high-gain edge.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic Marshall-era 4x12 cabinet sound.
Slightly scoop the low-mids while maintaining presence and punch (addressing 'reduce mid-scoop' correction).
No wah needed for dry thrash tone.
Minimal delay for occasional fills, kept mostly off to maintain dryness.

alternatives.reason: Too warm/ambient; Digital Delay is cleaner.

blocks.purpose: Minimal room ambience to prevent the tone from sounding completely sterile, but kept low.

alternatives.reason: Too much reverb for a dry thrash sound.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR for better definition and punch in fast, palm-muted thrash riffs.

proposals.reason: Enhance low-end definition and punch for tight, fast thrash riffs.
